messages.content: CK2 roleplay. Not a ruler yet. Son of Baron-Burgher (or whatever it's called in the land I'll choose) somewhere in what will be HRE (give options, close to Saxons). Year 769. I'm Ray, 16, boy. Immediate goal - to grow up, get education, learn from father, but not forget about normal life of teenager of this time. Long-term ambition - to inherit, develop my land, and maybe become Count, or even Duke (native names of titles)

Year 769. The Frankish–Saxon frontier is forests, marches, little timber castles, smoke from longhouses, and the first crosses of bold missionaries. You’re Ray, 16, heir to a small holding. You want to learn from your father, live a teenager’s life, and set yourself up to one day be called Graf… maybe even Herzog. ⚔️📜

Pick your start (all are in what will become the Holy Roman Empire, close to the Saxons)

A) Hessengau frontier (around Fritzlar, north Hesse) – castle-born
- Culture/Religion: Franconian (German) / Catholic
- Liege chain: Graf (Count) of Hessengau → King Karloman I (Karling)
- Father: Freiherr Gebhard von Fritzlar, castellan of Burg Fritzlar (baron-tier castle)
- Vibe: Real borderland. Missionaries pass through to Saxony; Frankish musters ride east. Expect drills, hunts, and early chances to prove yourself in levy duty.
- Good if you want: War, Hunting, Business (managing stores for campaigns)

B) Thuringian hill-country (Eichsfeld / Unstrut) – castle-born
- Culture/Religion: Thuringian (German) / Catholic
- Liege chain: Graf of Thüringen → Karloman I
- Father: Burggraf Ludolf von Gleichen (castle lord responsible for the local burg)
- Vibe: Mixed woodland and good farmland. Timber rights, tolls on a small trade road, simmering trouble with nearby Saxon Ostfalen. A builder’s playground.
- Good if you want: Business, Stewardship, Hunting

C) Westphalian March (near Eresburg) – Saxon tribal
- Culture/Religion: Old Saxon / Germanic pagan
- Liege chain: High Chief of Saxony (tribal)
- Father: Häuptling Wulfhard of the Eresburg Hills (chief of a fortified village)
- Vibe: Longhouses, spear drills, raids and reprisals. Charlemagne’s pressure is mounting; the Irminsul stands in the groves. High risk, high drama.
- Good if you want: War, Intrigue, bold frontier storytelling

If you’d rather be a city kid:
- A′) Hessengau market-town (Fritzlar) – city-born
  - Father: Bürgermeister Hartmut (mayor-tier city)
  - Vibe: Ledgers, tolls, fairs, guild talk; still must send men to the Graf.
  - Good if you want: Business, Carousing, Intrigue

Native title names (so you can dream properly)
- Baron (castle): Freiherr or Burggraf
- City lord: Bürgermeister (Mayor)
- Count: Graf
- Duke: Herzog
- King/Emperor for flavor: König / Kaiser

Your starting kit (customizable)
- Age 16; about to “lock in” an education. Likely paths:
  - Brilliant Strategist (Martial), Grey Eminence (Diplomacy), Midas Touched (Stewardship), Elusive Shadow (Intrigue), Mastermind Theologian (Learning)
- Suggested early traits (tweak as you like):
  - Diligent, Gregarious, Ambitious; maybe Patient or Brave if you want a push
- Lifestyle Focus options (pick one to start):
  - War, Hunting, Business, Family, Carousing, Intrigue, Scholarship, Theology

Long-game ladder to Graf/Herzog
- Serve your liege and stack prestige: lead levies, excel at council jobs (Steward or Chancellor are great for a baron’s heir).
- Marry smart: look for claims or alliances; a betrothal to a count’s daughter or an heiress can be your golden ticket.
- Build up home: improve palisades/keep (martial) or markets (stewardship). Money is leverage.
- Make friends: Carousing and festivals win allies; you’ll need backing for title grants or claim presses.

Ready to begin? Choose:
1) Your backdrop: A, B, C, or A′
2) Castle son (Freiherr/Burggraf) or City son (Bürgermeister)
3) Your Lifestyle Focus at 16 (War, Hunting, Business, etc.)
4) Any must-have personality traits

Then I’ll drop you into the first scene—dawn at your holding—with three immediate choices that shape your education and your teenage life.
